subject: Vegan Super Contract - Initial Feedback
body:
David,

Thank you for forwarding the contract.

Following our recent conversation regarding exclusivity, I wanted to share
a few items for your consideration. The points below reflect my notes from
January 22 and are intended to help ensure we are aligned as we move
forward.

First, given the proposed non-exclusive nature of the distribution
arrangement—and the fact that both Vegan Super and Cafuné will be entering
the U.S. market for the first time—I would like to propose waiving order
minimums during the first year. At the six-month mark, we could jointly
review performance and, based on initial learnings, establish appropriate
minimums for the subsequent twelve-month period. I believe this approach
allows both teams sufficient time to build awareness, test assumptions,
and gain meaningful insight into each brand’s market response before
formal commitments are set.

Separately, please confirm whether you would prefer the agreement to be
exclusive. If exclusivity is established, there would be no need to define
specific distribution regions within the U.S. In either scenario, I would
request that Warehouse Club and MarMaxx Companies be added to the list of
approved channels through which Beauty’s Lyric may distribute product.

With respect to minimum purchase requirements, I would also ask that you
consider waiving the first-year minimum purchase/forecast in light of the
upfront time and investment required to build awareness and infrastructure
(including DTC and Amazon). If a minimum is necessary, I would suggest a
$50,000 commitment in year one, with incremental growth of approximately
50% annually over the following two to three years.

Additionally,  please advise whether the brand owners currently carry
product liability insurance and, if so, whether U.S. territory coverage
can be added?

Lastly, if available, I would appreciate receiving a standard brand order
form.

I believe this captures my initial thoughts. Thank you very much, and I
look forward to your feedback.

Best regards,

Neil

subject: RE: RE: RE: Exploring U.S. Market Entry - Initial Questions
body:
Dear David,

Thank you very much for the detailed update — this is extremely helpful and 
appreciated.

The path you’ve outlined makes complete sense, and I’m very comfortable 
proceeding in the sequence you’ve suggested, beginning with Vegan Super, 
followed by Cafuné, and then the remaining brands as readiness allows. That 
feels both practical and thoughtful given the current status of each brand 
in the U.S. market.

Regarding Cafuné, could you please let me know who the trademark attorney is 
that you’re currently working with? I’m happy to support or help 
facilitate communication if that’s useful in moving the process forward.

For Vegan Super, I’d also appreciate confirmation on whether all trademark 
work for the U.S. market is fully completed, or if any remaining steps are 
still in progress. Having clarity there will help ensure a smooth and 
uninterrupted rollout.

One additional item for you to consider when you have an opportunity: given 
the non-exclusive nature of the proposed distribution and the fact that 
Vegan Super and Cafune  will be entering the U.S. market for the first time, 
I would like to propose waiving order minimums for the first year. At the 
six-month mark, we could jointly review performance and then set appropriate 
minimums for the following twelve months. I believe this approach allows 
both teams the time needed to develop the most effective strategies, test 
assumptions, and gain meaningful insight into each brand’s market response 
before formal commitments are set.

I’m very much looking forward to receiving the samples for Vegan Super and 
Cafuné and to taking the next steps together once they arrive. This feels 
like a strong starting point, and I’m excited to begin progressing 
in-market in a thoughtful and deliberate way.

Thanks again, and I look forward to continuing the momentum.

Warm regards,
Neil

Dear David,

Thank you once again for taking the time to meet with me yesterday evening. 
I truly appreciated the opportunity to connect and discuss the potential 
partnership.

I look forward to continuing our conversation regarding non-exclusive 
distribution for the Cafune, Vegan Super, and Dercent brands. While the 
distribution would be non-exclusive, my objective is to secure placement 
across Amazon, TikTok and Instagram Shops, key online retailers, and 
brick-and-mortar retailers headquartered in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast 
regions of the United States.

As discussed, Amazon will be a key focus. I will be collaborating with a 
team of specialists with extensive experience in building brand stores, 
creating A+ content, managing advertising strategies, and optimizing search 
visibility through targeted keywords. I have partnered with this team for 
several years, and together we have successfully achieved our KPIs with each 
brand we’ve managed.

Given the non-exclusive nature of the proposed distribution and the fact 
that these brands will be entering the market for the first time, I would 
like to propose waiving minimums for the first year. At the six-month mark, 
we can review performance and then set appropriate minimums for the 
following twelve months. This approach will provide time for both teams to 
develop the most effective strategies and gain insights into each brand’s 
market response.

Attached, please find my comprehensive résumé, outlining my career in beauty 
and skincare, including references to brands and accomplishments. My 
experience includes launching brands with Costco, Target, and Kohl’s, as 
well as overseeing brands in Walmart.

Once again, I would like to mention that I can be available for ‘market 
projects’ for any of the brands which you manage.

subject: RE: Exploring U.S. Market Entry - Initial Questions
body:
David:

Continue to be excited by the prospects of working together….

As we think thoughtfully about what a potential U.S. distributor 
relationship could look like, I wanted to ask a clarifying question to 
ensure alignment from the outset.

We understand that you may currently have broker relationships in the U.S. 
market, and that there is some limited existing distribution in place today. 
As we evaluate the scope of responsibility and investment required to 
represent the brands effectively, it would be helpful to understand whether 
those broker relationships would conclude upon the appointment of an 
exclusive U.S. distributor.

Additionally, we would appreciate clarity on whether any existing U.S. 
distribution relationships would be transferable to our company as part of a 
distributor appointment, and whether those relationships would transition 
without ongoing obligations, commissions, or “strings attached” to any 
third-party brokers.

Our goal in asking is simply to ensure a clean and transparent foundation, 
allowing us to invest fully—strategically and financially—in building the 
brands in the U.S. market with focus, consistency, and long-term intent.

We are, of course, very open to discussing any nuances or context around the 
current structure and welcome your perspective on the best path forward.

Many thanks, best regards,

Neil

subject: Exploring U.S. Market Entry - Initial Questions
body:
Dear David,

 

I hope this message finds you well. Thank you again for the thoughtful
conversations we've had so far - we're genuinely excited about the
potential to introduce the Muzigae Mansion, Efilow, and Midha brands to
the U.S. market and believe there is meaningful opportunity to build
awareness and traction thoughtfully and sustainably.

 

As a next step, and in the spirit of ensuring alignment before moving
forward, we wanted to share a short checklist of high-level questions.
These will help us assess feasibility, pricing structure, and a realistic
go-to-market approach for the U.S., particularly during an initial
market-entry phase.

 

High-Level Questions

1.	Tariffs / Duties
Do you understand current U.S. inbound tariffs on South Korea-origin goods
to be approximately 15%?
(Please let us know if your understanding differs or if you have recent
experience shipping into the U.S.)

Do you have any issue with U.S. distributor incorporating tariff into
suggested retail pricing?

 

2.	Global / Regional Pricing Policy
Is there a worldwide or regional pricing policy that a U.S. distributor
must adhere to (e.g., MSRP, MAP, or channel restrictions)?
If so, are there any flexibilities for initial market entry, sampling, or
awareness-building phases?

 

3.	Current International Distribution
For each brand, could you share:

*	Markets where the brand is currently distributed
*	Channel mix (e.g., DTC, specialty retail, department stores,
professional/spa, marketplaces)
*	Any reference points you can share regarding success in those
markets (strong retail partners, standout launches, meaningful growth, or
key learnings)

 

4.	Samples & Trial Sizes
Are samples available for each brand - ideally sachets or packettes - that
could support press, influencer seeding, professional outreach, and early
consumer trial?

 

5.	Hero & Best-Selling Products
For each brand, could you please identify:

*	Best-selling SKUs
*	Products you feel are most important for brand storytelling in a
new market
*	Any items already performing well internationally, if applicable

 

6.	Order Minimums (MOQs)
Could you please advise on order minimums by SKU and by brand?
We want to share, candidly and respectfully, that we are hoping there may
be flexibility or no minimums initially, as this allows us to:

*	Build brand awareness responsibly
*	Test product-market fit
*	Avoid over-exten

פי בקשתם.

2. שיווק - במידה והקוראנים ירשמו כיבואן, כולל חבות מוצר צד ג' ואחריות 
ביטוחית באחריותם, אז אכן הם יכולים לפעול שיווקית על פי רצונם.    לגבי ספר 
מותג  - אין לנו בשלב זה. כל תהליך הכנת הגרפיקות יגובה על ידי אנשי רגולציה 
שלנו מול הצוות הקוראני ונשמח שיתייעצו איתנו לפני ההשקה וקמפיינים ונוכל לעזור 
וחדד את המסרים ואת רוח המותג המקורי.

3. בעייתי מבחינתנו סינגפור לפתרון מחלוקות משפטיות  -  אנחנו לא יכולים לוותר

בדיוק מה ניתן לעשות ואיך, אנחנו נעבוד מולו גם במהלך החג על מנת לקדם דברים.

<‪david@yogico.kr <mailto:david@yogico.kr> ‬‏>:‬

Thank you for sharing the agreement.

The following is my opinion before sharing it with Nlize.

1. The agreement should be shared in Word file so Nlize can edit, give 
feedback and write comments on the file. It will be appreciate if Word file 
can be shared.

2. Marketing

Marketing: All marketing activities and materials must receive the Company’s 
prior written approval. The Distributor shall not register any trademarks, 
domain names, social media handles, or other identifiers similar to the 
Company’s in Korea.

Obviously, 99% of marketing activies and materials will be in Korean and 
there is no reason Company must receive them and approve beforehand. The 
following is better terms and may sound more reasonable.

-> All marketing activities and materials undertaken by the Distributor 
shall comply with the Company’s brand guidelines. The Distributor shall 
not, without the Company’s prior written consent, register or attempt to 
register any trademarks, domain names, social media accounts, or any other 
identifiers identical or confusingly similar to those of the Company in 
Korea.

3. Governing Law

In many cases of intentional agreements, based on my experiences even with 
Israeli companies, the governing law is a neutral country such as Singapore 
and not Israel and Korea.

This may sound more fair, logical and even "global company-like" in my 
opinion.

->This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the 
laws of Singapore. Any disputes shall be subject to the exclusive 
jurisdiction of the competent courts in Singapore. The application of the UN 
Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG) is 
expressly excluded.
